editorial:
If you grew up watching the Russo family cast spells and get into trouble, this TV movie feels like a warm reunion with an extra twist. Alex is trying to prove she is mature and responsible, but her impatience gets the better of her. She casts a spell to remove her bad qualities, and instead splits herself into a Good Alex and an Evil Alex. The setup is simple and fun, and it gives the story a clear good-versus-bad engine that kids and nostalgic fans can follow easily. The tone stays light and silly, with plenty of slapstick and family banter, so you never feel weighed down even when the stakes get big.

The acting is the real highlight, especially seeing one performer play two very different versions of the same character. The pacing moves quickly, bouncing between comedy and action without dragging. On the downside, the plot is predictable and some jokes land better than others. Still, it is a breezy watch that works great for a family movie night. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want to own it.
endingExplained: In the final battle, Good Alex faces Evil Alex, who has teamed up with a dark wizard to take over the world. Good Alex realizes she cannot win by being only good, so she accepts her flaws and merges back into one complete Alex. With her full self restored, she defeats the dark wizard and saves her family and humankind. The movie ends with Alex more confident and mature, having learned that her imperfections are part of who she is.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family fantasy comedies and nostalgic Disney Channel movies.
